meta.title: The demo, end to end — a machine is refused, a face changes the rule

views.label: Refused before any gas
views.note: The agent reads the indexed rules, works out that one intent cannot pass, and never sends that transaction.

views.label: Widening needs a human
views.note: A face scan produces a proof; the RP signs an EIP-712 attestation only after World returns 200; the blob widens the rule onchain.

views.label: The rule changed, not the agent
views.note: Nothing was redeployed or restarted. The agent's next tick simply reads a different world.

lanes.label: Agent loop — no key, no funds
Human in the loop — only for widening

phases.label: Refused before any gas is spent
The rule changed; the agent did not

edges.label: payee not on the allow list
a human decides to widen the rule

cards.title: What this beat is actually showing
items: A machine wants to spend, the rules say no, one human's face changes the rules, and the machine notices on its own
Nothing was redeployed, restarted or reconfigured between the refusal and the payment
The rules were never in a place the agent could reach

cards.title: Why the agent refuses itself
items: decide() is pure and reads only the subgraph, so it costs nothing and can be wrong only in the safe direction
It admits what it cannot see: the per-tx cap, the token allow-list, the time window and pause are not indexed — only the chain can confirm
So will-pass is a prediction, and the chain remains the authority

cards.title: The honest limits
items: A World proof cannot prove it came from Selfie Check — credential_type returns "device" either way, so the human-in-the-loop guarantee is configuration-level, not cryptographic
max_verifications: 1 binds to (person, action), so one World action can be scanned exactly once by the same person
The wallet key can still transfer directly and bypass all of this; that is the owner's escape hatch, not a hole
A block does not revert — it emits SpendBlocked and returns, so a successful receipt is not a successful payment
